body.statement: Almost surely, the constrained and unconstrained GCM slopes differ only on a finite contact interval at every \(x\), the integral \(D(x)\) is finite and nonnegative, and \(D\) has a separable locally bounded stationary version. Moreover, the joint contact radius for all \(x\) in a bounded interval has a tail sufficient for independent truncation of well-separated Brownian blocks.
body.justification: The continuum maximum and any declustering rule are meaningful only after the nonlocal GCM energy is localized and given a separable version.
body.gap: Banerjee and Wellner (2001) prove the one-point LR integral is well defined; the uniform contact-radius and local-boundedness statement for the translated field is not supplied there.
body.consumer: Finite-dimensional stationarity is available, while simulation and block separation still need separability and a quantitative common contact-radius tail.

obligation.what_is_open: A locally bounded separable version and a quantitative common contact-radius tail over compact sets of constraint locations have not been constructed.
obligation.obstruction: Parabolic drift localizes individual variational pictures but does not alone control every remote supporting chord for both constrained one-sided GCMs uniformly over a continuum; the target also leaves the required tail strength unnamed.
obligation.attempted: Brownian translation and affine GCM equivariance prove exact finite-dimensional stationarity, but an argmin-only bound does not control remote supporting chords.
obligation.partial_result:
Whenever both GCM energies are well defined, exact finite-dimensional stationarity follows.  For \(x,t\in\mathbb R\), define
\[
\mathbb W_x(t)=\mathbb W(x+t)-\mathbb W(x).
\]
Then
\[
X(x+t)-X(x)-2xt=\mathbb W_x(t)+t^2.
\]
Affine equivariance of greatest convex minorants and the substitution \(s=x+t\) imply
\[
D(x)=\Phi(\mathbb W_x),
\]
where \(\Phi\) is the origin-constrained Brownian--GCM energy.  Stationarity of Brownian increments gives, for all \(m\ge1\), \(x_1,\ldots,x_m,h\in\mathbb R\),
\[
(\mathbb W_{x_1+h},\ldots,\mathbb W_{x_m+h})
\stackrel{d}{=}
(\mathbb W_{x_1},\ldots,\mathbb W_{x_m}),
\]
and hence the finite-dimensional distributions of \(D\) are translation invariant.  This identity does not construct a locally bounded separable modification or bound a common contact radius over a continuum of constraint locations.
